cards.title: Approve the changed void-model check on sparky-1 (once, for every future release)
cards.plain: Release 1.3.0 added three packages to the install set for the DGX Spark. One approval lets the agent test it there. After that, the check follows each new release with no further approval.
cards.why: The check you approved on 2026-11-13 (A-02) was pinned to tag `v1.2.1-offline-arm64`, so each release needed a new approval. A changed command waits for you before any runner gets it.

sub: It asks GitHub for this repo's newest tag named `v*-offline-arm64`, and stops if there is none.
It fetches the repo at that tag into a temp folder and runs `tools/target_check.sh`.
It removes the temp folder afterwards.

steps: Press **Approve**. The agent then starts it and reports the result here.
cards.verify: The task shows **active** on the Tasks page. Its next run prints `release v1.3.0-offline-arm64` and ends with `PASS`.
cards.blocks: Confirming release 1.3.0-offline-arm64 on the DGX Spark (issue #4).

cards.title: Mask pipeline: a local Gemma server is the default; Google's Gemini API is opt-in
cards.plain: One pipeline step asks an AI model what a removal affects. It now uses a model on your own machine by default, so footage is not sent to Google.
cards.chosen: Stage 2 of the mask pipeline asks vLLM on `127.0.0.1:8000` serving `google/gemma-4-31b-it` (the model the README already downloads). Ollama, llama.cpp and Gemini are one option away (`--vlm-backend`); `run_pipeline.sh` passes it through. Gemini's key is read from the file named by `GEMINI_API_KEY_FILE`. Until this change stage 2 crashed on start and needed a Google key even for a local server (issue #4). Released in 1.3.0-offline-arm64. Details: `docs/SECURITY.md`, "Mask pipeline: where footage goes".
cards.why: The project's purpose is to run fully offline (README). vLLM's address was already the code's fallback for local servers, and it serves the Hugging Face model id unchanged, so no extra name has to be configured.
cards.if_ignored: Nothing to do: confirm, or overturn if you want Ollama (or Gemini) as the default instead.

phases.label: Fixed: kubric 0.1.1 in data_generation/requirements-kubric.txt until 2027-02-11
phases.note: Gone from the report on 2026-11-13. no release since 2021-08-25 (newest 0.1.1), over 3 years. Accepted until 2027-02-11: kubric 0.1.1 (PyPI, 2021) has no OSV advisory (checked 2026-11-13). It runs only in the optional offline synthetic-data generator (data_generation/kubric_variable_objects.py), never in inference or training. Upstream ships Kubric as its Docker image (kubricdockerhub/kubruntu) rather than PyPI releases; moving the generator to that image pinned by digest is tracked on the void-model BUILD board.

phases.note: Gone from the report on 2026-11-13. no release since 2021-06-14 (newest 0.6.0), over 3 years. Accepted until 2027-02-11: decord 0.6.0 (last release 2021) has no OSV advisory (checked 2026-11-13). It reads training videos only (videox_fun/data/dataset_*.py and the MPS reward), never at inference. Replacing it with a maintained decoder (torchcodec or PyAV) changes the training data path and needs a GPU training check: tracked on the void-model BUILD board.

phases.note: Gone from the report on 2026-11-13. 1 requirement(s) not pinned with == (decord): their versions are not known, so OSV was not asked about them. Accepted until 2027-02-11: The one line dep-audit reads as unpinned is the ARM64 decord wheel, a PEP 508 direct reference to the project's own release asset (v1.0.0-offline-arm64) pinned by #sha256=22c1b634… (stricter than ==: pip refuses any other file). Every other line is ==. void-model tests/test_security.py fails on any new unpinned line, so this exception cannot hide one. about.what: An offline, ARM64-ready edition of Netflix's VOID model: removes objects from videos together with the physical effects they cause (shadows, falls, collisions), built on CogVideoX.
about.why: The upstream VOID release depends on cloud APIs and x86 binaries. This edition runs fully offline on DGX Spark (ARM64, Ubuntu 24.04), with a local Gemma model for mask reasoning and a prebuilt decord wheel, so video inpainting can run without sending footage to a third party.
about.who: chappa.ai and researchers who run video object removal and its training or synthetic-data pipelines on their own GPU hosts, especially DGX Spark.
